cases.input: Moderator: To summarize absent resident Sol Pine, their issue was parking and they requested a garage study.

CHAIR: We will resume with construction logistics. Elena Marrow, a resident from West Cedar, is recognized. After Ms. Marrow, Rowan Pike, the project manager, may respond.
ELENA MARROW: Thank you. I have lived on West Cedar for seventeen years. The development itself is not what troubles us. The concrete trucks have been coming through the residential entrance at 5:30 in the morning, and the reversing alarms wake the whole block. Could the project route those deliveries through the Harbor Avenue entrance instead? That street reaches the site without passing the apartment courtyards.
CHAIR: Mr. Pike, please answer only for the project team.
ROWAN PIKE: We checked that route with our traffic engineer yesterday. Beginning next week, our team will route all concrete deliveries through the Harbor Avenue entrance. The smaller service vans will still use the existing gate during normal daytime hours.
ELENA MARROW: That change would address the early-morning problem. I appreciate the direct answer.
CHAIR: The clerk will record the logistics change. We are not opening the separate parking item yet.

MODERATOR: The next item concerns the Harbor Row housing proposal. I am calling Tessa Bloom from District 2, followed by planning commissioner Noel Hart.
TESSA BLOOM: I rent two blocks from the site in Harbor Row. The revised drawing keeps the family-sized apartments, which is important, but it moves the public courtyard into permanent shade. I support the housing proposal only if the courtyard stays on the south side. Could the commission restore that part of the earlier design before voting?
NOEL HART: The commission has not chosen a final layout. We may ask the architect to compare both courtyard locations, and we will consider the resident's condition during deliberations. I cannot promise a redesign tonight.
MODERATOR: To be clear, the project address shown on the slide is 20 Example Plaza. That is the development site, not Ms. Bloom's home.
TESSA BLOOM: Correct. Harbor Row is the area I gave for the record. My support remains conditional on keeping usable sunlight in the courtyard.
MODERATOR: Thank you. The written comment period stays open through the date already posted on the website.

CHAIR: We are moving to drainage near the North Quay works. Samir Vale, a shop owner from Market Bend, has the floor. The construction parcel is 88 Example Street.
SAMIR VALE: Water from the temporary ramp runs across the Market Bend storefronts whenever it rains. Yesterday it reached the entrance to my shop. Please clear the blocked drain and place a barrier along the ramp before the next storm. I am not asking you to change the project entrance.
CHAIR: City engineer Lio Frost, can you separate the immediate work from the later study?
LIO FROST: Yes. Our maintenance crew is clearing the blocked drain tomorrow morning. We will inspect the ramp after that, but the barrier needs a field measurement before I can give a date.
SAMIR VALE: Clearing the drain tomorrow is the urgent part. The parcel number on the agenda is not my business address, and I want the record to reflect that.
CHAIR: It will. The unrelated question about the bus shelter belongs under the next agenda item.

MODERATOR: Public comment continues with Jae Linden, resident of Pine Terrace in District 5.
JAE LINDEN: When I submitted my written comment last month, I supported closing the service road to cars. After watching the emergency-access demonstration this afternoon, I oppose a permanent closure. An ambulance should not have to wait for a removable barrier. I could support a weekend-only closure if emergency vehicles retain direct access.
MODERATOR: The record will show that the speaker changed the position stated in the earlier letter. Transportation director Mira Wren may respond.
MIRA WREN: The department might test a weekend-only closure, but we have not approved one. We will publish the emergency-access measurements on Thursday so residents can review the same information we used.
JAE LINDEN: Publishing those measurements will help. Until then, my position is opposition to a permanent closure, not opposition to every possible pilot.
MODERATOR: Thank you. A comment quoted from an absent neighbor will be entered as written testimony and not as Mr. Linden's statement.

CHAIR: I will call Mina Shore first and Mira Shore second. Mina Shore is the tenant representative for Lake Court; Mira Shore is the environmental consultant for the applicant.
MINA SHORE: Residents at Lake Court can smell diesel exhaust in the interior courtyard during overnight generator tests. The notice says testing can continue until midnight. Could the applicant finish generator testing before 9 PM and post the remaining test dates in the lobby?
CHAIR: Thank you. Mira Shore, please do not answer for the property manager.
MIRA SHORE: Our air study concerns daytime construction equipment, not the overnight generator schedule. The contractor told me, "We will finish by nine," but that was not a commitment made by my consulting team. I can submit the completed air-monitoring report to the clerk on Tuesday.
CHAIR: Contractor Daren Quill, can you address the schedule directly?
DAREN QUILL: Yes. Starting tomorrow, our crews will end generator testing before 9 PM, and we will post the remaining test dates in the Lake Court lobby tomorrow afternoon.
MINA SHORE: Those two steps answer the residents' request.
CHAIR: The clerk has captured the commitments from Mr. Quill, not the quoted statement from Ms. Shore.
